item.title: (Why|Who|Where) Rust - DebConf 26 [Spanish]
item.description:
For decades, systems programming has meant choosing between safety and performance. As our core infrastructure grows more complex, the cost of memory bugs and concurrency issues keeps climbing. This talk looks at how Rust fits into modern open-source development.

We’ll start with why Rust is gaining ground. By looking at common C/C++ pitfalls — iterator invalidation, undefined behavior, lack of thread safety — we’ll show how Rust’s borrow checker and type system catch entire classes of bugs at compile time. We’ll also walk through how Rust could have prevented real-world failures like Heartbleed.
item.content:encoded:
For decades, systems programming has meant choosing between safety and performance. As our core infrastructure grows more complex, the cost of memory bugs and concurrency issues keeps climbing. This talk looks at how Rust fits into modern open-source development.

We’ll start with why Rust is gaining ground. By looking at common C/C++ pitfalls — iterator invalidation, undefined behavior, lack of thread safety — we’ll show how Rust’s borrow checker and type system catch entire classes of bugs at compile time. We’ll also walk through how Rust could have prevented real-world failures like Heartbleed.

Then we’ll look at who is actually using it. Rust is already in the Linux kernel, and organizations like Google, Microsoft, Canonical, Discord, and Cloudflare rely on it in production. These aren’t experiments — they show the language is ready for the kind of infrastructure we maintain every day.

Finally, we’ll talk about where to get involved. The Rust community is active and welcoming, and we’ll share resources for finding support, contributing to open-source Rust projects, and connecting with other Rustaceans.

item.title: Rust for .NET developers [Spanish]
item.description: In this session, we will explore how .NET developers can transition into the Rust ecosystem. We’ll examine the core differences and similarities between C# and the Microsoft stack. By contrasting familiar .NET patterns with Rust-specific concepts—such as ownership, the borrow checker, and memory safety.

item.title: Creating an authorizer in AWS with cargo-lambda [Spanish]
item.description: In this session, we will explore how to leverage cargo-lambda to develop and deploy custom AWS Authorizers. The authorizer is used as an example to show how easy and performant is to use AWS lambdas with Rust.

item.title: Rust workshop: Build your own ls command [Spanish]
item.description: Presentation of the self-guided workshop by oxidar.org. The workshop is designed to be interactive: to pass each stage, the user must create a pull request against the main branch. Test are automatically run in a GitHub actions pipeline and if all tests are successful, the user is allowed to work on the next stage.
